title: Workflows or agents: who owns the control flow?

items.stem: Your team sketches four designs for handling a student's request in the makerspace assistant. Which one is a fixed workflow?

options.text: The model reads each question and picks which tool to call next
Your code always checks the calendar, then the model writes a reply
The model picks each tool, but only from a list of three
Your code runs each tool the model requests until the model finishes

items.stem: A program sends each student question to a model, which labels it "manual" or "booking". An if-statement in the program then runs the fixed series of steps written for that label. Is this system a workflow or an agent?

Every booking in your makerspace must follow the same steps: check the student's training record, check the calendar, then reserve the slot. The training check must never be skipped. The student picks the machine and time on a form. Which design and reason are best?

options.text: An agent, because three tools are involved and tools require an agent
An agent, because a firm prompt guarantees the check always happens first
A workflow, because fixed code can handle any request a student types
A workflow, because the steps are known and none may be skipped

items.stem: For the same kind of request, your fixed workflow makes exactly 2 model calls and an agent design makes 5 model calls on average. Assume every call costs $0.005 (half a cent) and there are 400 requests per week. How many more dollars per week does the agent design cost than the workflow?
Your agent lets the model choose each tool call until it writes a final answer. A teammate says, "We added a 10-step limit in our code, so it is now a fixed workflow." Which reply is right?

options.text: Agreed, since code that can end the loop also owns each step
Agreed, since a run with a known maximum follows a fixed path
Disagree, since the model still chooses each step within that limit
Disagree, since only removing all of its tools could make it one

items.stem: Which makerspace task gives the strongest reason to use an agent rather than a fixed workflow?

options.text: Diagnosing a failed print, where each finding decides what to check next
Sending each student the same confirmation message after a booking is saved
Building a weekly report by running the same five queries in order
Looking up one machine's opening hours in a table and showing them
